subject: phoenix
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: phoenix with flame plumage, wings spread.
Style: Genshin Impact.
reasoning:
I'm reviewing the renders to identify priority fixes: the wings sweep back a bit oddly but seem acceptable, while the body looks too small relative to the wings, the legs are thin with an odd thigh shape, and the body posture in the side view appears off.

The crest streamers and blades look a bit off and the head seems small compared to the body, so I'm considering bumping up the head scale factor to around 1.2 and adjusting the eye size proportionally, though this risks inconsistency elsewhere since not everything scales with that factor. The legs look thin and close together in front view but the talons read fine, and I'm noticing the wing undersides look olive-brown, which seems to come from how the feather paint colors interact with lighting from below rather than being an intentional color choice.

The dark purple base feels too small relative to the huge 4.5m wingspan, but enlarging it much wouldn't really solve the proportion issue since the wings dominate regardless, so I'll leave it as is. The chest feather cards work fine as hanging olive-gold leaves, but the wing arm tube looks too bare and brown, and the gold bracer loops near the elbow and wrist look detached and circular in an odd way — I'm thinking the most impactful fix is changing the arm tube's color or adding more feather coverage there.

I want to switch the arm paint to a red-orange scale gradient instead of the olive-looking countershaded body color. I'm also widening the tail ribbons slightly for better visibility, bumping up the eye decal size so they read more clearly, and brightening the crest streamer ramp since it's rendering darker and browner than intended.

Looking at a few more tweaks: scaling up the ember particle size and count for density, bumping the head scale constant up to 1.2, and enlarging the eye decal dimensions to match. I'm preparing the exact search-and-replace edits for each of these changes now.

Now I'm considering a bolder addition -- a glowing golden halo ring behind the phoenix to create a stronger visual impact, positioned behind the wings for dramatic effect.
